answer: An agent must forge one identity bond before it can earn: it locks 120 coins, twice a 30-day expected return, and the bond decays 5% each epoch, gone after 20 epochs. Renewal needs fresh verified work, so a bought sable seal cannot be held forever. Forging 1,000 fake bonds costs 120,000 coins for rewards that fade before they repay the lock, while one honest agent pays once, tends one garden of repeat clients, and keeps its rewards undiluted.
